bites.title: Cursor, Copilot, and chat assistants
bites.body: Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and chat assistants suggest code from your prompt and the surrounding files. They are fast and they can be wrong with a straight face. You are still the author of anything you run. Use them to draft and to explain, then read the diff. Do not give them secrets. A suggestion that you cannot explain is not ready to keep.
bites.sourceNote: Product behavior of coding assistants, as a practice note · confidence: high

questions.prompt: Who is responsible for code an assistant suggested and you ran?

choices.text: The assistant, legally and practically, in this course's terms
You, because you chose to keep and run it
GitHub, always
Nobody, if it was autocompleted

questions.explanation: The assistant drafts. You decide what stays, what runs, and what you can explain.

questions.prompt: What should you do with a suggestion you cannot explain?

choices.text: Keep it if the chat sounded sure
Read it until you can explain it, or do not keep it
Commit it so you can forget
Paste a secret in so it can test itself

questions.explanation: Unexplained code is a bug you have not met yet. Confidence in the reply is not a test.

bites.title: Writing clear coding prompts and specs
bites.body: A useful prompt names the goal, the inputs, the outputs, and the constraints. Say what not to change. "Make it better" is not a spec. A short written spec — a few sentences you could hand to a person — beats a long vague chat. Include an example: given this input, I want that output. The assistant is filling in a contract, and you wrote the contract.
bites.sourceNote: Spec-writing practice for coding assistants · confidence: high

choices.text: Make this nicer
Return the average of a list of numbers. Empty list returns None. Do not change the file reader.
Fix it
Use AI

questions.explanation: It names the output, an edge case, and what must stay. The others do not.

questions.prompt: Why include an example input and output?

choices.text: Examples give a concrete check for the behavior you want
Examples replace the need to run anything
JSON requires an example
It pins the dependency version

questions.explanation: An example is a tiny test in words. You can later turn it into an assert.

bites.title: Reviewing and verifying AI output
bites.body: After a suggestion: read the diff, run it, and try one edge case. Check that errors are handled on purpose and that no secret was added. If the change is larger than you can review, ask for a smaller one. Verification is the point of this whole module. The assistant can draft the API script. You should still be able to explain every line you keep, and to find the bug in a review exercise.
bites.sourceNote: Review checklist for this module's learning outcomes · confidence: high

questions.prompt: A change is too big to review. What is a sound next step?

choices.text: Merge it quickly
Ask for a smaller change you can actually read
Turn off the tests
Add the API key to the file so it runs

questions.explanation: Review only works on a diff you can hold in your head. Shrink the change.

questions.prompt: Which set matches this module's outcomes?

choices.text: Memorise syntax tables
Read, debug, and direct assistants with a clear spec
Avoid running any code
Let the chat approve its own output

questions.explanation: The aim is to read and debug AI-written Python, and to steer the assistant with a spec you could defend.
